topic: GP referrals to community mental health teams

audits.title: Making Sense of the Urgent GP Referrals; Audit Into How Many Are Actually Urgent?
audits.standard: Trust policy: all urgent GP referrals contacted within 48 hours by the duty team
audits.setting: Community mental health duty team, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board

cycle1.result: Only 13/124 urgent referrals were deemed urgent after telephone assessment; 53 referred to primary care mental health, 24 to secondary CMHT, 20 to older adults, 10 discharged to GP.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations: GP surgery visits to raise awareness and a brief risk assessment to justify urgent referral. Compliance with 48-hour contact was not reported.
audits.citation: Junaid M, Habeeb B. Making Sense of the Urgent GP Referrals; Audit Into How Many Are Actually Urgent?. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(S1):S159-S159. doi:10.1192/bjo.2022.450.

audits.title: Audit on the Assessment of Patients by the Primary Care Mental Health Practitioner at the Brentwood Community Centre and Subsequent Referral Pathways from January 2023 till January 2024
audits.standard: All new referrals first seen by the Mental Health Practitioner; MHP PCN Consultation V2 assessment template used; target 100%
audits.setting: Community Mental Health Team, Brentwood Resource Centre

cycle1.result: Referrals initially assessed 69.2% (82.5%); GP referrals compliant 67.2% (80.2%); MHP assessment template used 100%

audits.other_findings: 190 (24.5%) did not engage and 44 (5.7%) had data unavailable.
audits.citation: Queen Oka I, Kurien A, Agrawal V. Audit on the Assessment of Patients by the Primary Care Mental Health Practitioner at the Brentwood Community Centre and Subsequent Referral Pathways from January 2023 till January 2024. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S264-S264. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10647.

audits.title: General practitioner ENT referral audit.
audits.standard: ICGP referral guidelines and standardised referral form (maximum 37 points)
audits.setting: ENT service, The Adelaide and Meath incorporating the National Children's Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Average score 16/37; referrer details 75.42% (paediatric) and 72.9% (adult); clinical information 34% and 35%; only 32 letters mentioned examination findings.

audits.other_findings: Patient details scored an average of 42% for both groups.
audits.citation: Oosthuizen JC, McShane D, Kinsella J, Conlon B. General practitioner ENT referral audit. Ir J Med Sci. 2015;184(1):143-146. doi:10.1007/s11845-014-1075-6. PMID: 24526577.

audits.title: A retrospective audit of referral letter quality from general practice to an inner-city emergency department.
audits.standard: Authors' nine-item checklist and NSW Agency for Clinical Innovation referral template (2013)
audits.setting: Royal Prince Alfred Hospital emergency department, Sydney

cycle1.result: Over 60% completion in 80.9% of letters against the authors' checklist and 6.3% against the ACI checklist.

audits.other_findings: Handwritten letters (11.9%) were poorer; fewer than half included results, psychosocial or vaccination history.
audits.citation: Nash E, Hespe C, Chalkley D. A retrospective audit of referral letter quality from general practice to an inner-city emergency department. Emerg Med Australas. 2016;28(3):313-318. doi:10.1111/1742-6723.12592. PMID: 27197892.

audits.title: Re-Audit of the Contents of GP Referral letters to General Adult Community Psychiatrists.
audits.standard: Checklist of most important referral letter items agreed by GPs and psychiatrists (items scoring 8 or more)
audits.setting: General adult community psychiatry, East London NHS Foundation Trust (Bedfordshire and Luton)

cycle1.result: Reason for referral in 95%; current physical health 24%; risk concerns 47%; treatment provided by GP 50%.

audits.intervention: Standardised approach to referral letters devised with involvement of GPs and psychiatrists.

cycle2.result: Current physical health 59%; risk concerns 79%; treatment provided by GP 71%.

audits.other_findings: Questionnaire response rate 70% for psychiatrists and GPs; past medical and psychiatric history also improved.
audits.citation: Odelola C, Jabbar F. Re-Audit of the Contents of GP Referral letters to General Adult Community Psychiatrists. Psychiatr Danub. 2017;29(Suppl 3):607-609. PMID: 28953838.
